Use `useLayoutEffect` when you must read or change the DOM before the browser paints, e.g. measuring an element to position a tooltip, restoring scroll, or anything where `useEffect` would cause a visible flicker. For everything else use `useEffect`, since layout effects block paint. It also warns during SSR, so guard it or use it only in client components.

A double post on Enter in an htmx form usually means two things are firing the request, for example hx-post on both the form and the submit button, or an hx-trigger that also reacts to keyup or click, so a native submit and an htmx request both go out. I haven't seen the template, so that's a hypothesis. The usual fix is a single hx-post on the form, plus `hx-sync="this:drop"` and `hx-disabled-elt` on the submit button as a guard.
Action: Open the add-hike form template in trailmix and check where hx-post and hx-trigger are set, then fix it; if you paste the form I can say right away.

That pattern usually means the CSRF token is no longer being sent with the request. If the token only lived in a form field or template block that stayed in the base template, the partial's form posts without it, so Django returns 403. I haven't seen your files, so this is the likely cause rather than a confirmed one. Fixes are to put `{% csrf_token %}` inside the form in the partial, or send the token in an hx-headers X-CSRFToken header on a parent element.
Action: Look at the partial and the base template to see where the token is rendered and how hx-post is configured, then fix it; if you paste the partial and the base template body tag I can confirm.

Middleware runs in front of every request, so Next defaults it to the Edge runtime: it starts almost instantly, can run close to users, and uses web-standard APIs. The tradeoff is that Node-only APIs (fs, many native or Node-dependent libraries) are unavailable. Newer Next versions let you opt into the Node runtime for middleware, but I'd check the version in use before relying on it.
Action: No code change; if you tell me what you want to use in middleware, I can check the Next version and whether it's possible.

AsyncLocalStorage carries per-request context (request id, user, org) through async calls without passing it as an argument, which is why people suggest it for logging and tracing. It has a small overhead, usually negligible per request compared with I/O, but I'd measure it if it sits in a very hot path.
Action: Keep waiting on the api test run; if you want, I can then use it to attach the request id to Sentry events.

Both transpile TypeScript on the fly, but tsx uses esbuild, which strips types without checking them, so it starts fast and handles ESM and CJS interop well. ts-node uses the TypeScript compiler (type checking by default, so slower) and its ESM support is fiddlier. With tsx you lose type errors at run time, so keep the typecheck step in CI. Also, I edited package.json by hand and the lockfile isn't updated yet.
